notes.title: Patch - 0.7 (Experimental)
notes.content:
Hello everyone!
First of all, thanks everyone for being so polite and patient while waiting for this patch. Simple things I thought would be done by January dragged out sooo long. This is something I never thought would happen. I was not expecting my kids getting sick that much, and neither being so tired from new work (sausage stuffing as it is apparently called in Sweden, when you are given tons of new things to learn). So it has been really hard getting work into the game.

But now finally done! So coming years, will only (at least mainly) be of minor-patches, one new ability, building, unit, etc. Even if it comes in a pack (frost- & fire magic, *hint hint*). So hoping 2-4 weeks patches as max, otherwise I will push up half-baked stuff if it still needs more time.


Patch 0.7 (Experimental)
This patch is for the experimental version of the game, so if you want to try it out, you'll have to switch the game-version to Experimental.
The Patch log/info is what was announced in the previous post, so those of you that have already read it, don’t have to read it again. But I also have some more changes as well:


Game versions
I’m adding a third game-version - Experimental branch! (Thanks @光天辉夜)

Branch - Experimental
This version (branch) will always be first in receiving new stuff, so this is the branch if you want to try out the latest stuff that I'm experimenting / working with, which can be super-unbalanced and buggy. But on the other hand, faster for me to implement suggestions from the community, and will also have rough balancing.

Branch - Testing
This branch will be for those that also want to try new stuff, but don't want them to be game-breaking (if so by bugs or balance), and can't wait until they reach the release branch.
So here comes the “approved” & with rough balancing - stuff from Experimental-branch, and will focus on balance and (hopefully) fix remaining bugs. (this was previously the "beta"-branch)

Branch - Release (Live / no-beta))
And lastly this branch is when things should be bug-free and well-balanced, for those that prefer to wait to play the game in "stable version". Couldn't rename it :.(, so it is the "None" in beta-participation (the default one).


Equipment
Equipment stats is now applied last, so if you have 100 mana *2.0 from Meta-upgrades (those in main-menu “Progress”), +25 mana from gear and lastly a *1.25 mana from in-game talent, so will it now be calculated: 100 * 2.0 * 1.25 + 25 => 100 * 2.5 + 25 => 250 + 25 => 275.
As it felt more natural that both meta-progression and talents "boosts your character, not his gear". It will however make talents in game look like they give wrong value, e.g. previous example so would you have 225 mana, and with x1.25 talent feel like it should be: 225*1.25 = 281.25, but instead give 275. It's more or less, you as a character grow stronger, so e.g. you agility-training shouldn’t change how much agility a gear gives (if it makes any sense?).
Maybe I will rethink how to use multipliers in game, or maybe gear won't give "flat" bonuses, and only multipliers. It is something I wanted to give a try at least, so please let me know your feedback and suggestions.
pro's
 more "world-logic" (as mentioned above)
 Much easier to balance
 Cleaner numbers (275 instead of 271.25 with example above (OCD approved! :P))
con's:
 weird calculations with multipliers gained in game (as mentioned above)

Semi-rebalance
Semi, as in the game is playable, but I'm working to change the game's "strength"-progress, to be additive multiplication, instead of multiplied multiplication (is that how you say it?).

Example: Atm. so are the player AND units growing in strength by x*y*z, so say you have 100hp, get x2 talent, now you have 200, then you get a x5 talent, so 200*5 => 1000hp. I've been trying to have it so, as it is read more naturally. But the issue appears much more the further it goes, e.g. the growth is extreme (exponential growth?) compared to a diminishing return for addition-bonuses.

For an example, enemies at start deal 6 dmg, have 70hp, at endgame 500dmg 5000hp, This is a big issue with making "everything else" keep up, e.g. your towers can hold for a good time vs first enemies, but crumbles soon as a end-game enemy looks in their direction, and can only tickle that enemy (An arrow should still hurt a super-strong enemy imo.).
And I don't want your buildings & units to have upgrades that you manually have to "keep up" such big gaps, (e.g. go from 70 -> 5000hp upgrades).

It also gives a game-issue facing low-"tier" enemies later, say you can push/attack two fronts, west & east. Both have increasingly tougher camps the further you go in respective directions. And when you finished go one way (and thus able to defeat tier 3 enemies), and then start to go other way, you will face Tier 1 enemies, then their units and structures will insta die from you & your allies, as you are so strong to be able to handle tier 3 enemies, which felt wrong.

So I’m Instead going for the "additive multiplication" (or what it is called), e.g.
100 hp +100% +400% +450%
=> 100 * (2.0 + 5.0 + 5.5)
=> 100 * 12.5
=> 1250 hp
before with multiplication (same example)): 100 * (2.0 * 5.0 * 5.5) => 5'500.




And as always, if anyone has another solution, suggestion or any feedback at all, so am I open ears and will I gladly discuss it. Bet there is bunch of better approaches that I’m not familiar with.

notes.title: Dev-log / Beta Patch 0.7 - Upgrades & Sub-Factions
notes.content:
Yoo hooo,

Was hoping to finish the patch before the end of this week, but sadly need a couple more days until it is done. But I thought I could combine the patch-notes with the state of the game “dev-log” at the same time. So if you only want patch notes, just scroll past the dev-log.

So, finally finished with overhauling loads of code for the game, so now the current lagging-issue should be finally fixed. It was a complex beast, and also added a “hard-coded” limit on the amount of enemies, so they won’t be able to become a swarm of enemies attacking you. The next patch will however not have a balanced game, as that takes a lot of time to get good, but I thought it can’t make the game any worse then its current state. But it will be pushed to the beta-branch first, as I’ve touched more than 50% of the game-code in this patch, so it can be game-breaking bugs I need to fix with this patch.


The Performance-Fix
But the “performance-fix” also comes with some nice changes, Factions and Sub-factions! So, now maps will not be “hardcoded” to be played the same way every time, I’ve added multiple systems to make it much easier to add variations, but I’ve not yet added so many “variables / variations”, but that is something that will now be much easier to add in upcoming patches. Which is something I’m going to focus on, as I think it will bring much replay-value to the game for the short time needed to add it. For an example, so will you face a sub-faction later in the maps. Which atm. Have different armies, but later will have even more differences, like a leader you have to face, using different tactics and, *drum-rolls* more factions of enemies AND allies!

So I got the code in place for supporting the game to allow players to choose which allied-faction to play with, and a throw with a dice, which faction(s) you will face on the map, these non-allied factions can be neutral, allied or hostile towards you AND towards other factions on the map. On top of that, so will the maps be more “fluid” vs “rigid”, so sometimes a place on the map can be deserted, other times the main base of a faction.

This actually took some time to get units to have abilities on top of their auto-attack, a resource (mana) and different ai-logic-patterns. But now it is finally implemented. So sorry for only adding a handful new enemies only, that aren’t super-special yet. But will at least give you an idea of my plan for the game.

Upgradable stuff
Finally possible to make your allies a force to be reckoned with, if you invest in them. So I’ve added a blacksmith building that houses upgrades for some of your units, and your Castle has upgrades to unlock more buildings, for example a Stable that will provide your allies with mounts (amount is seen at top-bar now, same as food & gold), to train your next footmen to become cavalry. Or a Mage Tower to train, well, mages.

I really liked the idea of the stables not just being another “unit-producing-machine”, but rather adding a new resource, mounts, to upgrade your army with better “equipment”. I’m also planning on a lot more upgrades, units & structures in the coming patches, and most of all, interesting upgrades, not just dull “+health or +damage” upgrades. And instead have upgrades/tech-trees that lock out other branches. 

New GameMode
I’ve also added a new game-mode, which will be the default (non-hardcore mode) now, so you won’t lose the game upon dying, instead you will be revived at a shrine near the starting-area. As I was not fond of the idea of playing a >45 min long game, and dying of a simple mistake like, battery of the keyboard dying, cat turning off the monitor, you lost focus for 0.5 sec. But it's not insta, and the player will get a penalty in attributes for each death. So if you die too many times, you will have no strength left in the end to make a difference. I’m thinking of adding game-difficulties like Easy, Medium and Hard, to make these penalties removed, weak or harsh as well as a bonus meta-progression-xp, to even more tweak the game better for each player.

The long delay
What took so long time with this patch release since previous patch, is as mention in previous post, things in real life not always being kind to us, so I’ve lost a couple of months of work-time on game dev. But also a fix to the known high-performance of units-detection system  (AI), but still wanted the game to support “large” armies fighting each other, which wasn’t a simple task (not Total-war size, but not a 10 vs 10 turn based strategy game either). 

I’m also not planning on adding any new “systems” for a while, until I have filled existing ones with much more content in it, e.g. more equipment, upgrades, units, factions, maps. Which is far over due, maybe will continue with this over 1-2 years before adding new systems to be honest. As it now aaaaalmost have all the system for my 1.0 vision of the game (three more small ones i know of).


And as always, please let me know if you think something is unbalanced / should be changed. For example, ideas of what “arsenal” (units, structures, "tools") a specific faction or sub-faction should have, Is something I would need a lot of help with. Really hard to come up with fun, and hopefully, unique, ideas.



Patch 0.7
Game mechanics

Changed so you don't lose the game upon dying, instead you are revived at a resurrection-shrine after a short delay.
Added Sub-factions to enemies, so now enemies can have different origins, so they can have different units, tactics, structures.
Added a Hard-limit on enemies, so they will no longer be able to fill the entire map of units (rebalancing is on its way as well, to allow the “frontline” not being an “ongoing battle” from start of the game until end, instead be two large armies colliding and much faster kill of each other.
Reworked & Polished the AI, which will greatly increase the game’s performance
One part is updating the AI-tool I used, which sadly also made the units having a bit of weird behaviour sometimes (saw two footmen fall in love with an archer, and never left its side). Which is something I will look into with the upcoming balancing-patches in coming weeks. 
The larger part was making the AI much smarter, mainly with how they check the vicinity for potential targets, but also as individuals.
Changed so region 2 is now split into two separate regions (the two hills in the beginning of the map).
You now auto claim all loot-chests on the map you haven't opened, when you are victorious.
A new Upgrade-system which some buildings will use, like the castle in the beginning. To improve your allies' potential significantly.
New buildings:

Blacksmith: upgrade your units
Mage Tower: train mages (casters with area-attacks)
Stables: adds new resource, Mounts! So if any are available, so will your footmen train to become cavalry.
Hardcore Difficulty - As I mentioned above, so will the new “game-style” where you will respawn upon death, maybe not be a game-style for you, so I added this setting in the Map-lobby, to be able to play like the old version (you only have one life). But I’m not sure how big (if any?) xp-bonus should be rewarded for meta-progression when having it on, as it is more difficult, so might just remove it, maybe remove it and down the road add achievements only gained by playing in hardcore? Let me know what you think.

Quality of Life

The food system will now also show Consumed / Produced above delta-food. To be more useful / explained.
Added gameplay setting to disable the delay when you close a window in game.
Added some red/green numbers on your stats, to easier see positive or negative values (top right when you open in-game menu or when picking a level-up)

Balancing

Market sells excess food twice as fast now, felt too far away with only once per minute, so it is roughly twice as strong (Think this one will need plenty of tweaks in future patches, so let me know what you think).
Most equipment are rebalanced, so "basic" items will no longer have negative values (e.g. the +hp regen ring, don't give -mana regen anymore).
Equipment with negative attributes are special cases that will be known as "Cursed" (Corrupted, Unholy?), which later will have a much stronger positive effect, but with a negative effect as well (curse), which are meant to make them feel pretty weak at first glance, until you combine it with right "gear" (class, faction, abilities, other equipment), so the negative effect can be reduced or even negated completely. 
This will make so there are “basic” equipment that are simple & plain “buffing” equipments, but I’m a bit in love with the idea of making equipments that have extreme penalty, which could be completely negated, e.g. lets say a equipment gives x2 damage buff, but stops your mana-regen / spells cost 10x more mana. Which don’t bother a playthrough if you have abilities that don’t cost mana.

Other

Moved the "lover's tree" (units got stuck on a specific tree close to the starting area)
Updated items & chest's visual effect and size, so they are easier to detect.

Bug fixes

Your money shown in the build-GUI was resetted when closing the build-window.
You were able to cast other abilities when using channelling-abilities, by just using the other ability twice.
You were able to reopen the in-game-gui when you had returned to the main-menu.
You weren't able to level up last picked ability.
Some sounds were still playing even when muting the game in GameSettings.
The game-over sound effect didn't always play.

Near Upcoming changes

A new map - I have some really fun ideas for it, so they will be much more fun to replay (higher replay-value), and i will stick to hand-made, instead of a “generic”-made procedural generated map.
 Factions - both enemies AND allies are going to have new factions added to be faced / played with, to even further add different playstyles and more randomness in how each match will pan out.

notes.title: Current status on Myriad Mayhem
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

This will be a long one, but a fast summary if you don’t want to read all: I ran out of money to work full time on the game, and will still work on it on free time, working on current patch, that grew very large (couldn’t find a easy fix), so it will take some time to release.

edit: The game will still be up on steam, the only thing that changed is I won't be able to put as much time into the game.


Sorry for keeping you all in the dark for so long, so I thought it is due time to let you know how everything is going. First of all, thanks for being patient with the game, for playing it and not least of all, coming with all the feedback (the good and the bad, as it helps me improve the game).

I have some good news, and bad news, so start with the latter. Sadly my saved money and loaned money ran out before I was able to make the game a “worthy game”, even tried to “make it work” by working 80 hours / week, but I couldn’t do that for longer than a month. So sadly I can’t work on the game full time anymore, but the game is so precious for me, so I will not put it aside before I at least finish my bare-bone vision of the game, which is years ahead.

So, I’ve been working on a patch that grows out of proportions, you all know the pathfinding-issue, and that is the big issue I’ve been wrestling with. After no fast solution, so did I instead buy a tool from the Unity market, which I thought would be a fast-fix. But, that tool also had major performance issues out of the box. And even weeks trying to tweak it to fit into the game, so it didn't help that much, even trying their experimental-version.

So, I instead thought of another solution to it, to postpone the issue, and is also things I’ve planned to add later into the game, so taking down two problems with one stone, and that is, adding more “power” to both allies and enemies, because now the end-game combat is more or less a standstill as units are produced faster than they die. Sure, in hindsight so could I just lower the amount of units spawned, but then I would spend time only patching an issue instead of fixing it permanently. Plus it would make the game boring to only have a few units in a fight (the performance issue is because of multiple units “detecting” hostiles and what is able to be attacked)

That brings us to the current patch / Good news! :D
So my philosophy is that I want talents & equipment to feel impactful (compared to +3% damage for 7 seconds for your “entire party” in a MMO). And that brings an issue, if you want to gain x30% more damage per talent for an ability, so do the enemy have to scale a lot to “keep up”, it all works if you are the only one dishing out damage (like Diablo), the problem is with your allies, then they also need to deal more damage over a game session to “keep up”, to avoid only being cannon-fodder end-game, or even less useful. So the upcoming patch is bringing an upgrade-system to the game and new units / buildings. 

 The starting castle now has technologies you can invest in to unlock new units and buildings. 
 Blacksmith: that you can upgrade your core armies (footmen, archers, cavalry)
 Stables: Supports your army with mounts, so your footmen will train to become cavalry
 Mage-Tower: train mages, which are like glass-cannon with area attacks

The enemy is also gaining stronger unit types that can dash out area-attacks. This will make the end-game battlefield have different types of units, not only weak “cannon-fodder”, but also these key-units to keep an eye out for, as they can decide the outcome of the battle. That also means, the enemy will deal much more damage = you are more likely to die, even more so if you focus on only offensive talents / equipment (glass-canon). Which brings the next issue, dying AND losing after a long game over a simple mistake / facing a new enemy (looking at you, nasty Vraal). So, I’m changing that you don’t lose upon dying, instead respawn at base, as long as your castle is still standing (You will still lose if the castle goes down as usual though).

This will make a >30min game not as irritating by dying by a simple mistake. (Maybe I’ll add a hardcore-checkbox option in the lobby, with maybe a +x% progression bonus, if that is something asked for).

Also added more ideas on what to bring to the game, which can be found in the Discord server https://discord.gg/R7sn7qRHYA (in #roadmap) 

But I was wondering, do you want me to create a Trello / post more often with updates on how “larger patches” are going, e.g. what is finished and what is remaining? It will however mean I will have to take time from working on the game, I could maybe do a summarized/small post each month to let people know how it is going?

I understand if some of these changes are breaking things you like with the game (e.g. no longer 1x life), but don’t forget, it is Early Access, so please let me know if it is so! As a solo-dev, so are your ideas worth gold. Maybe you see a good adjustment for a new issue, an option to enable/disable a new feature, or in worse case, remove a new feature that just made the game worse (put it on a shelf, for maybe a adjustment that could fix it)

notes.title: Beta Patch - 0.675
notes.content:
Trying out a new food-system, let me know if you prefer this one or the old one. It removed the complexity of having a "current storage / max storage" of food, and buildings having different updating intervals.

Game mechanics

notes.title: Live - Patch 0.6
notes.content:
Finally 0.6 is here!
It contains a few fixes & minor changes, but most of all, it contains a Base-building system!
It's still in an early phase, so nothing is written in stone and can change if something feels bad.
So, the map is divided into regions, which your allies will put guards on already, if a region is mostly cleared of enemy structures.
Now, you will also see building plots become visible in cleared regions, these come in three sizes, Small, medium and large.
And structures will then be categorised into these sizes. So structures fit into specific sizes (small structures fit in small plots, medium structures in medium plots and large structures in large plots), you can however always fit a smaller structure in a larger build plot if you so like.

Structures
Watch Tower - A basic defensive structure, which will attack enemies
Small Farm - Produce food and also increase food storage
Barrack - Train troops to attack your enemies.
Large Farm - Same as small farm, but more of both
Marketplace - Generate a small amount of money, but it's a unique structure (can only have one marketplace), and the reason for being unique is it will sell all excess food you produce.
Stronghold - A fortified defensive structure, which will attack enemies

The Food System
So you might wonder, what is all this about "food" he speaks of? Well, it's the first step of a new resource-system I'm aiming for, so it might feel a bit wanky atm, but will of course be polished & adjusted down the road. So the way it works is that your allies troops now need food to be trained, so if you run out, they won't train any more troops.
And troops on the map will also eat food with certain intervals.

Structure-system insight
So the first idea was to only make farms / economic-structures only produce money, but it was so stale, simple, but kinda boring. So I thought this was a nice solution to it. So later you may get better gold-generating structures, but then still need food to keep those hungry soldiers fed. And it kinda is the same anyway, as soon as you have a Marketplace, it's more or less like the food == money in current state anyway.

Updated Info
Made a new trailer, screenshots and updated the Steam Store Page to reflect the current gameplay, as it changed so much since the release version.

Increased game-price
Increased the game price to 6.9€ to match the game current state, I'm a fan of Factorios approach to marketing, so I will not have a sale on the game as I want to pay respect to every purchase of the game, and as a gamer, so do I know the sour taste of buying a game for 80€ and 1-2 weeks later the game gets a 75% Discount. So I will make it so you can avoid that completely.
That's the reason why I didn't even have a Launch-sale of 10-20% that most do, but it was baked into the 4$ price-tag.
So I'm sorry if you think the game is priced too high, so only buy the game now if it intrigues you or you want to support the development of the game. If not, then I hope I can convince you in the future when I've had more time to develop the game to be convincing value.

The future
So now I don't have any large new systems to implement in the near future. And instead focusing on getting rid of the last known bugs, fixing the Units AI (getting stuck and what not), adding more content and finally balancing the game.

Game mechanics

 Base-building System!
 Food-system

 Added so enemies structures drop xp as well.
 Added so you start by default with two rerolls & one banish.
 Added so you are slowed 50% when casting MagicMissile.
 Changed so metalevels now have 5 levels by default instead of 2, was a bit boring to only spend one point per level, but to strong to get more gold to upgrade more then one per levelup.
 Added a Tower to the barbarians you face.
 Added so if you attack enemy's structure it will awake the whole camp (enemies buildings are in groups)
 Changed so all dropped xp will now last forever from start, don't need to find & buy the ItemDuration MetaProgression upgrade (and it is also removed)
 Rework on MagicMissile:

 MagicMissiles is now affected by Quantity,
 Relocated MagicMissile talents in its talent-tree
 Removed MagicMissile is affected by Talent-Duration and no longer get speed-upg on its own talent, as that combined with the updated Talent-Speed, made your missile fly far outside the screen (e.g. can sniper enemies structures from super-safe distance, might want a sniper-ability later, but not MagicMissile at this stage).
 Removed so it has same amount of tiers of talents as remaining abilities (MagicMissile had one more tier then rest) In the future, i might go back and make all abilities have more talents, but atm. so is the game lacking in the amount of abilities, which i want to remedy first.

 Added a boss "event"
 Added sound when you awaken enemies camps.
 All units now have a low health-regen. Which is felt needed for units on guard-duty.


Quality of Life

 Updated so XP-orbs visuals, e.g. now they are Green - blue - yellow - red, felt more natural to green beeing weaker. And lowered their VFX-effect.
 Changed so normal scrolling combat text last 50% longer.
 Changed so Crit-text last 3x longer.
 Added red effect on screen when getting low health
 Added camera-shake when you critical hit.
 Added scrolling combat text when your health/mana is restored (by non-regen sources).


Balancing

 Updated so most tougher enemies now gives more xp.
 Updated so the xp needed for ingame lvling is roughly 20% lower, e.g. you level faster at higher levels.
 Updated so you level progression-levels much faster (need better name for these, Rank?).
 Updated Flash so it reaches twice as long, and takes roughly 40% shorter time to reach its destination.
 Updated ChainLightning to be roughly 70-80% higher dmg, but made it cost 20 -> 40, I wanted it feel more "impactful" not an spamming-ability.
 Changed place on which levels you unlock Flash and MagicCircle talents with progression-level (MagicCircle feels more helpful, so more fun getting it earlier).
 Balanced all abilities
 Made the game easier.
 Boosted multiple talents effect, to have larger impact
 Rebalanced the Progression talents.
 Removed Quantity from Progression-talents (those seen in main-menu), might re-add it later, but was hard to balance current abilities with it available.


Other

 Updated the map.
 Added death sound to all units and structures
 Rewrote the whole AI logic system.
 Added so projectiles like arrows will play a on-hit sfx when they dissapate (hit ground).
 Added clouds to the game
 Sadly there are some bugs with units start wiggle when a structures is destroyed, sadly its a game-engine issue with the pathfinding which I can't find a solution for. So I am going to check for other tools to replace the built-in-pathfinding-system.
 Changed name on Progression-value Gold -> Coin (you will get gold in another way later, hint hint).


Bug fixes

 Fixed so beam won't hit friendly targets.
 Adjusted Sounds, as when you get to many sounds, some will cancel out others. So now every sound have a specific priority, so it isn't as easy to notice (appears you can only play x-amount of sound-effects atm. Gonna look more into it, if it remains an issue).
 You shouldn't be able to get talents that aren't improving either you or your abilities

notes.title: Patch 0.345
notes.content:
Here comes another patch!
First of, now allies will help with attacking!

secondly, I've Re balanced the whole game!
So bumped up all health & damage on everything, and also health-regen. Mainly so the Talent Damage will have larger impact, as +40% damage wouldn't increase MagicMissile's 1 damage (only working with whole numbers). Plus it felt kinda "weak" to only do 1 1 1 1 damage when using MagicMissile. However, I really like low numbers like D&D, compared to games that you start with doing one-two digit-numbers, but in end-game do millions of damage, it feels weird, especially on such low scale-scenarios.
So that's why it was so low from the start, i wish i could keep the low numbers, but the only other way was to start working with decimal numbers, but dealing 2.141 dmg looks bad in my opinion.

However,
I do know there are some animation-bugs on units, and sometime they just stand still, which is something I'm working atm. But after consideration so will all these new features weight way more then a few new bugs. As I assume most of you want to experience.
And I was thinking in the future to make a beta-branch with these "in-between" versions. But right now, so do I think this time, it makes the game so much better.
Plus I know the game spike in difficulty after some part into the game, and that is the next system/feature I'm working on, that will make those spikes manageable.

Hope you will enjoy it, best of luck adventurers!

Game mechanics

 Your allies will now help you with sending out troops to attack enemies fortifications.
 Added so units will hit if they start their attack-animation, to avoid player griefing enemies by walking away before they trigger dealing damage.
 Added more enemies


Balancing

 Updated Talent.Pickup-radius to increase size from 0.125 -> 2.0
 Increase Allies castle's attackrange from 15 -> 20
 Decreased Bandits spawning frequency


Other

 Made buildings projectiles larger, so they are easier to see
 Changed so scrolling-combat-text (damage numbers) are only shown if they are made by the player or affecting the player


Bug fixes

 Fixed bug with saving & loading game-resolutions

notes.title: Patch 0.340
notes.content:
So here comes a bigger patch, I wasn't prepared the game would be so easy. Both with the characters leveling speed and strength. So had to tone them down, The main reason is for the allies which are arriving soon. Otherwise will the first enemies and allies at start become trash-mobs really fast, which isn't an approach I'm after.


Game mechanics

Added a barely visible ring to show pickup-radius for the player.
Allies Castle regenerate hp slowly
The level-up window will now show your current level at top left corner
XP orbs was hard to see behind tree's, so changed they use same Silhouette shader as enemies (red behind stuff), which is a bit logic, as the xp is dropped by them.
Changed friendly silhouettes are yellow instead of cyan (was hard to see behind tree's)


Balancing

Balanced the whole game, so the player won't grow in strength so fast as before.
Decreased hp regen a lot, as it was way to powerful
Increased how much xp you need to gain Character-progression-levels, but you will still keep your gained xp up until now (no xp reset).
Changed so Bandits Stronghold (largest spawn building) spawn two times slower


Other

Changed the xp-save/load system to easier balance changes to how much xp is needed for lvling
When you can't level up anymore (out of talents to pick from), it will say "Max Level!" at bottom left, instead of its ordinary text (I didn't think it would be so easy gaining max-level in previous version)
Changed mana-bar color, was a bit hard to see as dark-blue.
Updated so talents will show 2 decimals, e.g. higher lvl beam could show increased value: Interval 0.2 -> 0.2 (it rounded to 1 decimal before) when it was 0.24 -> 0.16.


Bug fixes

Fixed bug with you could obtain a Talent not yet unlocked by progression-level.
Fixed bug with MagicMissile-Accumulator and Flash-Surge of Speed didn't always apply their StatusEffect.
